title: Running in Docker and what the kernel gives it
one_liner: A container is just Linux processes with fences around them, so PostgreSQL still needs the same kernel gifts: files, shared memory, semaphores, sockets and signals.
analogy: A container is a rented room in a big building. The building (kernel) still supplies the plumbing and power. The room only limits how much you can use, such as a small /dev/shm closet.
big_picture: The official image starts as root, fixes folder ownership, then uses gosu to become the postgres user (uid 999) before running initdb or the server.
PostgreSQL refuses to run as root (check_root in src/backend/main/main.c) and wants the data directory to be mode 0700 or 0750 (checkDataDir in src/backend/utils/init/miscinit.c).

Shared buffers use mmap shared memory by default on Linux (shared_memory_type = mmap). Parallel queries use dynamic shared memory from shm_open, which lives in /dev/shm. Docker gives only 64MB there by default.
Docker stops a container with STOPSIGNAL. The image sets SIGINT, which the postmaster treats as fast shutdown. Plain SIGTERM would mean smart shutdown, which waits for clients.
The server itself needs no special Linux capabilities. The entrypoint needs CHOWN, SETUID and SETGID while it is root, and sometimes DAC_OVERRIDE and FOWNER for mounts it did not create.
In the 18 image, PGDATA is /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker and the VOLUME is /var/lib/postgresql. Older images used VOLUME /var/lib/postgresql/data.

flow.detail: ENTRYPOINT is docker-entrypoint.sh, CMD is postgres. The script sees uid 0.
mkdir -p PGDATA, chmod 00700, chown to postgres. /var/run/postgresql is created with mode 3777 in the Dockerfile.
exec gosu postgres re-runs the script as the postgres user, so the server never runs as root.
If PGDATA has no PG_VERSION, docker_init_database_dir runs initdb --username=... --pwfile=<(printf ...) using POSTGRES_PASSWORD, plus POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS.
pg_ctl starts a server with listen_addresses='' (unix socket only) and runs /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/* (.sql piped to psql, .sh run or sourced). Then pg_ctl -m fast stops it.
exec "$@" replaces the shell so postgres is PID 1 and gets the stop signal directly.
check_root, checkDataDir (permissions), then shared memory (mmap) and semaphores are created.
Docker sends SIGINT. The postmaster maps it to a fast shutdown: abort sessions, checkpoint, exit.

diagram.claim: A docker run goes from a root entrypoint, through gosu, to a postmaster that asks the kernel for memory, semaphores and sockets.

key_files.what: check_root refuses to run as uid 0 (unless --version/--help style flags come first).
checkDataDir: owner check and mode must be 0700 or 0750.
Main shared memory: anonymous mmap, huge pages (MAP_HUGETLB), small SysV key for locking.
DEFAULT_SHARED_MEMORY_TYPE is MMAP on this platform path; SHMEM_TYPE_SYSV and MMAP enum.
Dynamic shared memory; POSIX variant uses shm_open and resizes the segment (error text: could not resize shared memory segment).
handle_pm_shutdown_request_signal: SIGTERM smart, SIGINT fast, SIGQUIT immediate.
max_files_per_process (default 1000), virtual file descriptors, debug_io_direct check.
Docs for kernel resources and Linux memory overcommit / OOM killer.
Defaults. The upstream sample says unix_socket_directories /tmp. The Debian image patches it to /var/run/postgresql.

interview.q: Why does Postgres refuse to run as root?
answer: A bug or malicious extension would then have full control of the machine.
check_root in src/backend/main/main.c prints a refusal and exits.
In Docker the entrypoint starts as root only to chown, then uses gosu to become postgres.
interview.trap: Running the container with --user root and expecting the server to start. It will not.

interview.q: What permissions must the data directory have?
answer: 0700, or 0750 if group read is wanted.
checkDataDir in miscinit.c rejects anything else with 'has invalid permissions'.
I ran it with mode 0755 and got exactly that FATAL plus the detail line.
interview.trap: Bind mounts from a host with a different uid or loose mode break startup. Fix the mount, not the check.

interview.q: Why does the Docker image have a VOLUME and what is PGDATA?
answer: PGDATA is where the cluster lives, in 18 it is /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker.
VOLUME /var/lib/postgresql keeps data outside the container layer so it survives removal.
Older images (17 and earlier) use /var/lib/postgresql/data as the volume.
interview.trap: Mounting an old-style path on an 18 image and thinking data persists.

interview.q: What does POSTGRES_PASSWORD do and when does it apply?
answer: It is passed to initdb through --pwfile, only on first init of an empty PGDATA.
Changing it later has no effect on an existing volume.
POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE works for Docker secrets.
interview.trap: Changing the env var and expecting the password to change.

answer: After initdb, a temporary server starts with listen_addresses='' and runs each file in order.
*.sql go to psql, executable *.sh run, others .sh are sourced.
Scripts run only on an empty data directory.
interview.trap: Putting scripts there and expecting them to rerun on restart.

answer: The postmaster maps SIGTERM to smart, SIGINT to fast, SIGQUIT to immediate shutdown (postmaster.c).
Smart waits for all clients to leave, so docker stop would hit its timeout and SIGKILL.
Fast aborts sessions and checkpoints cleanly. I sent SIGINT to a scratch server and saw 'checkpoint starting: shutdown immediate' then 'database system is shut down'.
interview.trap: SIGKILL or immediate means crash recovery on next start.

interview.q: Why do parallel queries fail with a 64MB /dev/shm?
answer: Parallel workers share data through DSM segments. With dynamic_shared_memory_type=posix these are shm_open files in /dev/shm.
Docker limits /dev/shm to 64MB by default.
When the segment cannot be resized you see 'could not resize shared memory segment ... No space left on device'.
Fix with --shm-size, or reduce parallel workers and work_mem.
interview.trap: Blaming shared_buffers. Main shared memory is a separate mmap, not /dev/shm.

interview.q: How does main shared memory differ from DSM, and what about huge pages?
answer: Main segment: shared_memory_type defaults to mmap on Linux, a small SysV segment is kept just for the interlock.
huge_pages defaults to try: MAP_HUGETLB is attempted and quietly dropped if it fails. 'on' needs mmap type and reserved host huge pages.
In a container, huge pages must be reserved on the host and allowed to the container.
interview.trap: Setting huge_pages=on in a container with no hugepage allocation, so the server will not start.

interview.q: What is double buffering and why does fsync matter in containers?
answer: Postgres caches pages in shared_buffers and the kernel caches them again in the page cache.
fsync (default on) forces WAL and data to disk so a crash does not lose commits.
Container memory limits (cgroups) usually count page cache too.
O_DIRECT is only exposed as the developer setting debug_io_direct.
interview.trap: Turning fsync off for speed on data you care about. Overlay filesystems do not make it safe.

interview.q: Why can the OOM killer kill Postgres in a container, and what helps?
answer: The cgroup memory limit makes the kernel kill the largest process when exceeded.
If a backend dies by SIGKILL the postmaster restarts all backends in crash recovery.
Docs in runtime.sgml suggest vm.overcommit_memory=2 (host setting) and sizing work_mem times connections carefully.
Set container memory above shared_buffers plus connections times work_mem.
interview.trap: Thinking the container can set vm.overcommit_memory. It is a host kernel setting.

interview.q: Which capabilities does it need, and how do sockets and ulimit fit in?
answer: The server needs none. The entrypoint typically needs CHOWN, SETUID and SETGID while root, sometimes more for existing mounts. Drop the rest.
Default listen_addresses is localhost, which is unreachable from outside a container, so the image config makes it listen on all interfaces. The init temp server uses '' (socket only).
max_files_per_process defaults to 1000 and Postgres checks the real ulimit -n at start; a low nofile limit shrinks usable files.
interview.trap: Assuming EXPOSE 5432 publishes the port. It only documents it; you still need -p.

contributor_tips: Compare behavior against docs: doc/src/sgml/runtime.sgml covers kernel resources and OOM.
When touching shmem or DSM code, test with a small /dev/shm or tmpfs to see the failure path.
Use a scratch cluster with pg_ctl -D tmpdir and a high port; never reuse a real data directory.
Keep unix socket paths short: my first run failed because the path exceeded the 103 byte macOS limit (Linux limit is 107).

more: Scripts in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d run only when PGDATA is empty. .sql.gz files are decompressed and non-executable .sh files are sourced.
Postgres is PID 1 in the container. Use docker run --init if you worry about zombie processes.
docker stop sends SIGINT (a fast shutdown), then SIGKILL after 10 seconds. Raise --stop-timeout when checkpoints are long.
Shared memory is anonymous mmap, so no SHMMAX tuning is needed. It still counts against the container memory limit, like page cache does.
The image listens on all interfaces, but the port is unreachable until you publish it with -p. EXPOSE is only documentation.
